The simulated serpentine manipulator had a total of 20 degrees of freedom.
The 13-ft mast had 1 degree of freedom (rotation ±180 degrees).
Stages 1-3 of the manipulator had 3 degrees of freedom each (pitch 0-45 degrees).
Stage 4 had 6 degrees of freedom (pitch ±30 degrees, yaw ±15 degrees).
Stage 5 had 6 degrees of freedom (pitch/yaw ±30 degrees).
The wrist had 2 degrees of freedom (roll ±180 degrees, pitch ±60 degrees).
The authors discretized the manipulator's workspace into a 21x28 ft. grid with 1 ft spacing.
The 2D grid was used to represent the full 3D tank environment by rotating the plane using the mast rotation.
The evolutionary strategy used a population of 1 and a mutation operator to optimize the joint configurations.
The authors had to manually adjust the mutation operator's initial variance and decay rate to achieve tight convergence.
Co-evolving the configurations to reduce both distance to target and joint-space penalties simultaneously was ineffective.
The final lookup table-based control system enabled accurate and continuous motion of the end-effector.
The authors' approach is applicable to 3D hyper-redundant manipulators, unlike much of the previous work.
The authors' method does not require computationally expensive techniques like the Frenet-Serret formulation.
The authors were able to easily incorporate various design constraints through the fitness function.
